doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Package tours and the original quintet
title: How Eric Dolphy joined the quintet
summary: Eric Dolphy appeared in Jazz on a Summer's Day; he came after Buddy and Paul Horn, recommended by Gerald Wilson, and Hamilton remembers him as a gentleman who fingered his horn constantly.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Well let’s go back to your appearance -- you know, they documented it on Jazz On A Summer’s Day up in Newport and you have Eric Dolphy on there. I know you mentioned that you started with Buddy, but when Buddy turned left on you brought Jerome Richardson out.
But on that film there’s Eric Dolphy on stage with you.
Eric is on that film. And between that time after Buddy, I think it was Paul Horn, yeah, and after – Paul, Eric.
So how did you come to meet Eric and how did he -­

Well Eric and my brother and his ex-wife, they all went to school together, you know, LA Junior College. You know, they all went to school together. Also Eric lived in the neighborhood, in the area, you know.
Are you talking about Jefferson High School or are you talking about junior college.
Would they have gone to Los Angeles?
Yeah, whatever it was. But anyway, when I needed a player -- I think Gerald Wilson told Eric, you know, to give me a call, you know, and right away we hooked up.
Did he come out and audition for you or did he just come in and do a gig?

No, he just came out and we started -- came in and started rehearsing, you know, that type of thing, which was cool. And it’s funny, not funny, but in a sense -- because Eric Dolphy man, was one of the nicest persons I have ever, ever known. Number one, he was a perfect gentleman and he was total music, total music. We’d be traveling, he’d be sitting back in the backseat of the car, he’d have his horns out. He wouldn’t’ have his mouthpiece going but he’d be fingering his horns. He was totally music all the time, man. And the way he went out man, was really too bad, you know. He was a diabetic and those fools over there thought he had been shooting up, the Germans, right. But Eric was dynamite, man. Beautiful dude.
